items.title: Russell Kofi Eni elected new President of AAG
items.description: Russell Kofi Eni has been elected as the new President of the Advertising Association of Ghana (AAG). He took over from outgoing president Mr. Andrew Ackah at the association’s 35th Annual General Meeting and Council Elections on Wednesday, 18th November 2026. Delivering his final presidential address, Mr. Ackah called for a deliberate programme of transformation to make the Association more visible, influential and financially sustainable. He said the night was not only about accounting for another year, but about reflecting on a journey and handing over the baton. “Four years ago, you gave me the privilege to lead. Today, I return that mandate with a deep sense of appreciation,” he said. LIST OF NEW AAG EXECUTIVES & COUNCIL MEMBERS 1. Russel Eni. President 2. ⁠Makaila Akuamoah. Vice President 3. ⁠Russell Banful. Treasurer 4. ⁠Sena Vuley Council Member 5. ⁠Linda Amofa-Agyemang. Council Member 6. ⁠Bright Ladzekpo. Council Member 7. ⁠Kwaku Danso-Misa. Council Member 8. ⁠Collette Amaeshi. Council Member 9. ⁠Justin Darkwah. Council Member 10. ⁠ Lynn Osei. Council Member 11. ⁠Yanfo Hackman. Council Member 12. ⁠Emmanuel Lamptey. Council Member 13. ⁠Joseph Andoh. Council Member Building on foundations Mr. Ackah said he did not inherit an Association without direction, crediting his immediate predecessors for beginning reforms to restore confidence at a time when there were concerns about AAG’s strength, visibility and influence. “Our responsibility was not to start again, but to build upon that foundation, accelerate the reforms and take the Association to another level,” he said. He said his administration set out to make AAG more visible, more contemporary, more influential, more financially sustainable and much more relevant to members and the wider industry. Rebranding and Membership Growth One of the most visible expressions of that transformation, he said, was the rebranding of AAG — not just a change of logo, but a change in how the Association presented itself, how people experienced it, and how members, partners and the business community perceived it. The Association introduced a modern website and strengthened its presence across social media, communicating more consistently with members and stakeholders. Membership also grew significantly. Over the period, combined corporate and individual membership increased by more than 60 per cent, with increasing diversity beyond advertising agencies. “Agencies will always remain at the heart of this Association, but the marketing communications ecosystem is much broader than agencies alone,” Mr. Ackah said. He cited organisations such as Ecobank Ghana Plc and The Coca-Cola Company joining AAG as a signal of what the Association must become — a broad professional home for organisations and individuals who believe in responsible, effective and creative marketing communications. Gong Gong Transformed Mr. Ackah said another major transformation was the Gong Gong Festival of Creativity & Awards.For decades, Gong Gong had celebrated creativity and excellence, but he said it could not continue to be presented in the same way year after year. The Festival was given a new image, expanded beyond the awards night, strengthened in positioning, and given a stronger commercial proposition. A dedicated Gong Gong Board with a two-year mandate was established to provide strategic leadership. Inaugurated in November 2025, the Board helped deliver an improved Festival in 2026 under the theme “The Creative Convergence: AI and Human Craft in Advertising.” This year’s Festival received entries from 22 agencies, with 146 entries shortlisted and 16 agencies winning awards. KPMG provided independent assurance around entries, shortlist and winners, strengthening transparency and credibility. Sponsors included Eskimi, Nutrifoods Ghana, Telecel Ghana, Ecobank Ghana, GB Foods and Blue Finance.“Gong Gong must become more than an awards night. It must become one of Africa’s respected platforms for creativity, innovation, professional exchange and industry recognition,” he said. Push for Advertising Bill On regulation, Mr. Ackah said the proposed Advertising Council legislation had received renewed government attention, with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Agribusiness and the Attorney-General’s Department engaging AAG in reviewing the Bill. He said the review was updating the Bill to reflect digital marketing, influencer marketing, online advertising platforms, artificial intelligence and other developments absent or insufficiently addressed in earlier versions.But he warned the work is not finished. “I strongly believe that the Advertising Bill should be passed before the current Parliament completes its term,” he said. “The industry needs an appropriate legal and regulatory framework that protects consumers, raises professional standards, creates clarity for practitioners and ensures that Ghana’s advertising environment keeps pace with changes in technology and business.” He listed the Bill as the top priority he is leaving for the incoming Council. Cannes Lions And Professional Development Mr. Ackah said AAG had also strengthened its international relationships, deepening its partnership with Lions, organisers of the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, with increased Ghanaian participation in the judging process. “Ghanaian creativity cannot operate in isolation,” he said. “Our professionals must increasingly see themselves as part of a global creative community.” On professional development, he said the Institute of Advertising Ghana, AAG’s training arm, had introduced a structured Continuous Professional Development programme this year — a 13-week programme for entry-level to early management professionals, complemented by masterclasses for senior managers and business leaders. The CPD, he said, is groundwork towards establishing a Ghana Advertising School to close the gap between academic education and practical industry skills. “The Ghana Advertising School must help close that gap,” he said. “Our vision is to create an institution that combines rigorous academic discipline with hands-on professional training.” He said preparatory work had begun for full accreditation from the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission, and the next administration must move the project decisively from preparation into implementation. Data Must Be Matched With Trust On the AGM theme, Mr. Ackah said clients are demanding greater accountability, boards want evidence of return, and technology gives access to unprecedented data.“But data alone cannot build a successful industry. Trust remains fundamental,” he said. “Clients must trust that agencies are giving them sound advice. Consumers must trust that brands are using their data responsibly. Agencies must trust that clients value their intellectual and creative contribution.” He said the strongest agencies of the future will be those that combine creativity with data, technology with human judgement and commercial ambition with integrity. Advice To Incoming Council Mr. Ackah outlined six priorities for the incoming President and Council to be elected that night: Keep the Advertising Bill as a top advocacy priority until it becomes law Broaden AAG membership to include more non-agency corporates, brands, media, technology companies and professionals Move the Ghana Advertising School from concept to reality Continue transforming Gong Gong to be more commercially sustainable and recognised beyond Ghana Strengthen relationships with professional bodies, regulators, educational institutions, government and international partners Continue giving young people a place in the industry through pathways, mentorship and opportunities to lead. A Relay, Not A Solo Race Thanking two Councils, the Executive Director and Secretariat, committees, the Gong Gong Board, member agencies, partners and past Presidents, Mr. Ackah said leadership is never a solo enterprise. “There have certainly been difficult moments. There were decisions that required patience. There were ambitions we could not complete,” he admitted. But he said he remained convinced Ghana has an advertising industry with enormous talent and potential, with creative people capable of competing anywhere in the world. “As I bow out as President, I do so with gratitude and with optimism,” he said. “I am grateful that we were able to leave AAG stronger, more visible, more respected and more ambitious than we found it.” To his successor, he said: “Lead boldly, but listen carefully. Protect what has been built, but do not be afraid to change what must change. Keep AAG relevant to its members. Keep raising professional standards. Keep building partnerships. Keep advocating for the industry. Keep developing our people.” “At some point, you must hand over the baton. Tonight, that baton will pass to a new President and a new Council.”

items.title: INEC backs code for independent tabulation of 2027 election results
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has endorsed a voluntary Code of Conduct for independent tabulation and publication of election results ahead of 2027. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the backing at a stakeholders’ roundtable convened by Yiaga Africa in Abuja. The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, states this in a statement he signed on Thursday in Abuja. According to Itodo, Amupitan, who was represented by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, said the code would strengthen transparency and public confidence. He warned that independently aggregated figures, projections and partial tallies must never be presented as official election results. “Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres of statutory authority,” the INEC boss stated. Amupitan outlined six guiding principles for the framework, including methodological integrity, accuracy, information integrity, data security, error accountability and voluntary compliance. Itodo said independent tabulation helps citizens to scrutinise election outcomes and assess credibility. The Yiaga Africa boss noted that differing methodologies and publication standards could cause confusion during sensitive collation periods if left uncoordinated. He stressed that a common code would establish minimum standards, curb premature declarations and ensure findings are backed by reliable verification. Itodo said Yiaga Africa was expected to lead further engagements to translate the agreed principles into a practical framework before the 2027 general elections. Participants at the forum included civil society groups, political parties, election observers, the National Broadcasting Commission and the Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria. Also in attendance were representatives of the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) and the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ). Stakeholders examined different tabulation models, including Yiaga Africa’s Processing Results Voter Tabulation (PRVT) and Election Results Analysis Dashboard (ERAD), alongside INEC’s Result Viewing Portal (IReV) aggregations. They agreed that organisations must clearly disclose their methodologies, data sources and margins of error to prevent public misinterpretation. A technical session also highlighted the need for human verification, audit trails, data security and transparent error-correction procedures. Media stakeholders emphasised the duty of journalists to verify figures and clearly distinguish independent tallies from official results declared by INEC. (NAN) The post INEC backs code for independent tabulation of 2027 election results appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ntim Fordjour accuses Mahama government of prioritising luxury jets over security needs
items.description: Ranking Member of Parliament for the Defence and Interior Committee, Rev John Ntim Fordjour, has accused the Mahama government of placing greater emphasis on luxury presidential aircraft than on addressing critical needs in the security sector. He claimed that while successive budgetary commitments to improve the welfare and operational capacity of security agencies had not been fulfilled, the government had found more than GH¢1.86 billion to acquire luxury presidential jets and helicopters. Speaking during parliamentary debate on the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy, the NPP MP questioned the government’s spending priorities, arguing that the investment in aircraft contrasted with what he described as persistent funding gaps across the security services. He said previous budget promises to pay accommodation allowances for security personnel, recruit additional officers and equip the security agencies had not been adequately delivered. He also cited the failure to acquire fire tenders for the Ghana National Fire Service, attack helicopters and air defence systems for the Air Force, as well as the necessary equipment to strengthen the Navy’s maritime operations. Beyond the security sector, Rev Fordjour argued that the government had also fallen short of commitments to create meaningful employment opportunities for young people and provide better prices for cocoa farmers. He alleged that the only sector experiencing significant growth under the current administration was cocaine trafficking, while traders, farmers, young people and other sections of the population continued to face economic difficulties. The MP called on the government to redirect spending towards pressing national needs, particularly security, employment creation and the welfare of personnel serving in the country’s security agencies. He further urged the authorities to intensify efforts against narcotics trafficking and ensure that security agencies received adequate funding to tackle illegal mining, violent extremism, terrorism and rising urban crime. Rev Fordjour said the 2027 Budget must be realigned with Ghana’s National Security Strategy, insisting that the government should prioritise the country’s safety and the operational needs of its security institutions over what he described as excessive spending on presidential travel.

items.description: Following the call for election issued by the FIFA Council on 29 April 2026, the FIFA general secretariat has received the following candidatures proposed by FIFA Member Associations for the presidential election that will take place at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco, on 18 March 2027. items.title: Ghana calls for coordinated action to strengthen child protection systems
items.description: The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, has called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, families, schools and communities to tackle violence against children. She said protecting children required a coordinated system that prioritised prevention, provided support to families and ensured timely responses whenever abuse or violence was reported. The Minister made the call at the Second Global Ministerial Conference in Manila, Philippines, during a session on strengthening child protection systems through a multi-sectoral approach. She emphasised that parental and caregiver support, safe school environments and effective response mechanisms must work together to guarantee children’s safety and well-being. Dr Lartey stressed that reporting channels must be backed by functional institutions capable of responding to cases and providing the necessary assistance to affected children. Highlighting Ghana’s progress, she said the Integrated Social Services initiative now covers all 261 districts, bringing together social welfare, health, education, justice and social protection agencies to improve case management and referrals. She also cited the training of 5,375 social workers, police officers and judicial personnel, alongside efforts to strengthen child protection laws and professionalise the social service workforce. On prevention, the Minister outlined interventions including the National Parenting Strategy and public education campaigns that have reached more than 3.5 million people. She added that every public senior high school now has trained Safe Space Focal Persons to support child protection, while efforts are underway to link school reporting systems directly to district social welfare services. Despite these interventions, Dr Lartey acknowledged persistent challenges, including shortages of trained personnel, dependence on development partner funding and fragmented data systems. She called for increased domestic investment, stronger accountability and better coordination to make child protection services more sustainable and effective. Drawing lessons from Ghana’s experience, the Minister identified the need to organise services around children’s needs rather than institutional boundaries, strengthen existing government structures, and invest in both the social service workforce and data systems. She said sustained collective action was necessary to ensure that prevention measures translated into lasting improvements in the protection and welfare of children.

items.title: Formation of electoral reforms committee delayed because opposition not finalising nominees: minister
items.description: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Thursday said the formation of the Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER) had been delayed because the opposition had yet to submit its nominees. He made the remarks after meeting opposition chief whip Malik Amir Dogar to discuss the committee’s formation. In a post on X, Chaudhry said the government and its allied parties had submitted all their nominees for the committee. “The opposition should finalise its nominees soon; the (National Assembly) Speaker will issue the notification to form the committee as soon as the names are received,” he said. Chaudhry further said that if the PTI wanted to return to mainstream politics, it should join the electoral reforms committee and present its position there instead of expressing reservations on talk shows and in the assembly. “PTI will have the opportunity to address its concerns about the upcoming elections in the committee,” he said, adding that the party’s “constructive proposals” would be incorporated into the final draft of the electoral reforms. Besides the next general elections, the committee can also discuss the current political situation, said the PML-N leader. “The government is providing PTI with a forum to present its position and electoral proposals,” he claimed. PTI decides to hold parliamentary party meeting PTI, meanwhile, has decided to convene a meeting of its parliamentary party to decide whether to participate in the PCER. According to a senior party leader, lawyers Latif Khosa and Salman Safdar did not recall asking party founder Imran Khan about the matter during their three-hour meeting with him. “If they had asked Imran about joining the committee, there would be no confusion, as PTI follows the directions of its founding chairman,” the leader said. However, PTI believes that, as in 2017, when an electoral reform process was undertaken, the government and opposition should have equal representation in the PCER to prevent one-sided decision-making. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn that a decision could not be taken because a meeting of the parliamentary party had to be held during a National Assembly session, but it had been delayed. “We also have to take the opposition parties into confidence on the matter. A meeting of the parliamentary party will be held soon, and coalition partners such as Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and others will also be taken into confidence,” he said. Akram further said Imran had directed party members not to become part of parliamentary committees of the National Assembly and Senate, but had issued no specific directions regarding the PCER. Therefore, a decision would be taken after deliberations at the parliamentary party meeting. Earlier this month, the government, taking ownership of an initiative to bring all parliamentary parties, including the opposition, to the negotiating table on electoral reforms, formally appr­oached its allies to join the proposed PCER. It had contacted its key allies, the PPP and the MQM-P, seeking nominations for their representatives on the proposed committee. The government also formally approached the opposition to seek its representation. However, the opposition had termed the formation of the committee a “futile exercise” unless its long-standing demands were met.

items.title: L’Indonésie envisage de rejoindre l’alliance militaire de l’Arabie saoudite, de la Turquie et du Pakistan
items.description: L'Indonesie pourrait devenir le premier pays d'Asie du Sud-Est a rejoindre le pacte de defense de La Mecque, signe le 7 août par l'Arabie saoudite, la Turquie et le Pakistan. Selon trois responsables turcs cites mercredi 18 novembre par Middle East Eye, Jakarta etudierait les modalites d'une eventuelle adhesion. Mais aucune demarche officielle n'a ete annoncee : l'ambassade indonesienne n'a pas confirme les informations. L'accord repose sur un principe de defense collective : une attaque armee contre l'un des trois signataires est consideree comme une attaque contre tous. Il prevoit aussi une cooperation accrue dans le renseignement, l'entraînement et l'industrie militaire. Pense dans un contexte de tensions avec l'Iran et d'attaques houthies contre l'Arabie saoudite, il pourrait elargir son influence au-dela du Moyen-Orient. La Syrie s'est montree interessee . La lune de miel entre Ankara et Jakarta Les liens militaires croissants entre les deux capitales expliqueraient l'interet. En 2025, l'Indonesie a conclu un contrat de plus de dix milliards de dollars pour acquerir 48 avions de combat turcs KAAN. Elle doit aussi recevoir deux fregates de classe Istanbul dans le cadre d'un accord evalue a un milliard de dollars. En octobre, elle a signe avec la Turquie, le Pakistan et le Qatar le pacte de Badr, consacre a la cooperation industrielle de defense, sans engagement de protection mutuelle. Mais une adhesion a La Mecque marquerait un tournant diplomatique. Le president Prabowo Subianto defend traditionnellement une politique etrangere « libre et active », qui permet a Jakarta de multiplier les partenariats sans rejoindre de bloc militaire. Il a lui-meme affirme ne pas vouloir integrer d'alliance de defense. Ankara tempere d'ailleurs les speculations. Le ministre turc des Affaires etrangeres Hakan Fidan a precise le 17 novembre que les trois fondateurs privilegiaient pour l'instant la consolidation du pacte, plutot que son elargissement. L'interet prete a l'Indonesie reste donc, a ce stade, une hypothese diplomatique.

items.title: Prince Harry says would rejoin military to fight Russia if needed
items.description: Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday. “I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the western city of Lviv over the weekend. “If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.” Harry, a former British army officer and the younger son of King Charles III, made his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion to meet wounded veterans and medics. The prince is also the founder of the Invictus Games for wounded veterans and met athletes hoping to represent Ukraine at next year’s games in the British city of Birmingham. “Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, that doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he told the British daily’s “Ukraine: The Latest” podcast. “I feel very confident that Europe has a united front, and it would be fantastic to have more American support for that as well,” he added. Earlier on his weekend visit to Lviv he told wounded veterans and medics specialising in war injuries: “You’re going to win the war”. He repeated that sentiment on the podcast, insisting that “Ukraine are winning” and “there is no version where Russia is making any more advances”. The 42-year-old prince has previously spoken about being moved by witnessing death and life-changing injuries while on deployment in Afghanistan, and launched the Invictus Games in 2014 when he was still in the British army. Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the UK earlier this year from California amid an enduring rift with the royal family and his brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William. But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online. Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images. items.title: Quarter of a Million Landmines Removed from Zimbabwe - The HALO Trust has destroyed four mines per person in north-east Zimbabwe
items.description: Countries: Zimbabwe, Afghanistan, Angola, Colombia, Sri Lanka, Syrian Arab Republic, Ukraine, Yemen Source: HALO Trust Harare, Zimbabwe, 19 Nov. The world’s largest landmine clearance charity, the HALO Trust, has reached a significant milestone in Zimbabwe, destroying 250,000 landmines since 2013. Dense belts of landmines, including the highly sensitive R2M2 models, were laid along Zimbabwe’s borders with Mozambique and Zambia during the Liberation War in the 1970s. They’ve killed or injured more than 1,500 people and 120,000 cattle since independence in 1980. For 13-years, HALO’s Zimbabwean teams have cleared these minefields in Rushinga and Mount Darwin, saving lives and limbs while restoring farmland, reconnecting communities and laying the foundations for investment and economic growth. “The destruction of 250,000 landmines is an extraordinary achievement, built on the dedication and courage of Zimbabwean men and women working in some of the country’s most dangerous areas” said Oliver Gerard-Pearse, HALO Trust Zimbabwe Programme Manager. In Rushinga, where losing a single cow to a landmine can cost a family the equivalent of six months’ school fees, clearance has directly benefited more than 14,000 residents, allowing families to reclaim farmland, graze livestock, grow cash crops and safely access clean water, schools, clinics and markets. ***“We would walk in fear”***saysresidentMunesa Takawira “Now, we are free to walk as we please, and the cows and other domestic animals that used to be hit by landmines can freely move around. We can send children to fetch firewood without fear that they will get injured.” In Mount Darwin, where HALO became the first operator to hand over an entire district as landmine-free in 2021, deaths and injuries from explosives fell to zero, incomes rose by 90% for nearly a third of local farmers, and land-owning families in six communities increased by more than 80%. As the largest demining organisation in the country, HALO also provides vital local employment in areas where jobs are scarce. The organisation trains female deminers who are often the main breadwinners for their families and support an average of eight relatives through their clearance work. Drones, state of the art detectors and mini excavators are helping HALO clear faster and more safely. But technology alone cannot fully counter the impact of sweeping global aid cuts, which threaten Zimbabwe’s aim to achieve mine-free status by 2030. Just 4% of land remains contaminated says Gerard Pearse who estimates that it would take $6.5 million in donations to free the country from mines by the end of the decade. “We have seen how safe land can boost investment and development in other countries where HALO works. In neighbouring Mozambique, GDP rose significantly when it was declared mine-free in 2015” he says. “In Zimbabwe we are now so close to lasting safety for generations to come. We cannot afford to lose momentum at this final stage of a decades-long effort.” Please find footage of our demining operations here and images here (credit: The HALO Trust) For more information or to arrange interviews or site visits, please contact media@halotrust.org Notes to editors Zimbabwe ranked second globally in anti-personnel landmine destruction after Cambodia, according to the Clearing the Mines 2025 report. HALO has trained over 17,000 adults and 73,000 children how to stay safe from explosives since 2015, working closely with Happy Readers, a local charity that provides children with educational books on the risks of mines. HALO also works with Cassim's Prosthetics to support amputees. The HALO Trust is the world's largest humanitarian landmine clearance organisation, working in in 30+ countries including Ukraine, Afghanistan, Yemen, Syria, Colombia, Angola and Sri Lanka. We deploy groundbreaking technology in conflict and post-conflict settings to help people rebuild their homes, restore their livelihoods and keep their children safe. HALO also runs programmes in weapons and ammunition management and safety training. During emergencies, we also provide humanitarian aid and logistical support. HALO was founded in 1988 in Afghanistan. We employ over 8,000 staff worldwide and recruit 95% of them locally.

items.title: Cameroon: North-West and South-West Situation Report No.87, July to September 2026
items.description: Country: Cameroon Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Please refer to the attached file. HIGHLIGHTS More than 1,600 protection incidents recorded in the North-West and South-West regions. Nearly 900 people displaced in the North-West and South-West regions due to violence and insecurity. More than 4,000 people affected by floods and landslides, with about 500 displaced and five deaths reported. Four improvised explosive devices incidents recorded in the North-West region. A total of 736 children with severe acute malnutrition received life-saving treatment in partner-supported treatment centres. SITUATION OVERVIEW / HUMANITARIAN ACCESS During the reporting period July-September 2026, the humanitarian situation in Cameroon’s North-West and South-West (NWSW) regions remained fragile and deteriorated further amid continued clashes between State security forces (SSF) and non-State armed groups (NSAGs). Persistent insecurity, including kidnapping for ransom, arbitrary arrests, the proliferation of illegal checkpoints, extortion, and roadblocks, continued to restrict population movements, hinder access to basic services and livelihoods, and heighten protection risks for affected communities. The situation remained volatile, with at least 11 improvised explosive devices (IED) incidents recorded during the reporting period, including 10 in the North-West and one in the South-West. While these attacks primarily targeted SSFs and their convoys, civilians remained at significant risk of injury or death from accidental explosions. Attacks and threats against education intensified ahead of the 2026/2027 school year. NSAGs enforced school-related restrictions, imposed school levies in some areas, and increased intimidation of education personnel, including the abduction of five teachers in Wum (Menchum division, North-West). In September, armed actors also attacked a secondary school in the North-West, disrupting learning activities. Humanitarian needs remained severe across the two regions, exacerbated by successive lockdowns imposed by NSAGs between 1 and 21 September. The measures restricted movement, disrupted education, livelihoods, and economic activities and limited access to essential services. Lockdown enforcement through threats and sporadic attacks resulted in civilian casualties in both regions and further affected already vulnerable communities. Continued clashes between parties to the crisis triggered new population displacement and humanitarian needs across the North-West and South-West. In Momo division, an estimated 875 people (175 households) were displaced from Diku to Tikom during the reporting period with many families seeking refuge in nearby bushes. Heavy rainfall that caused flooding and landslides on 5 August affected over 4,157 people, displaced more than 500, caused five reported deaths, including a pregnant woman, and destroyed or damaged 16 houses infrastructure, livestock, and community water systems in Limbe (Fako division), Kumba (Meme division) in the South-West, and in Tinifoimbi Village (Boyo division) in the North-West. While many affected households have returned, those whose shelters were destroyed or damaged remain displaced and in need of assistance. Priority needs include shelter, food assistance, health, WASH, protection, education and livelihood support. In coordination with OCHA and area-based coordination co-chairs, humanitarian partners delivered multipurpose cash assistance, shelter support, psychosocial services, and gender-based violence prevention interventions across affected communities, in addition to the assistance delivered by authorities. Humanitarian access remained constrained due to insecurity, prolonged lockdown and the presence of illegal checkpoints along key road corridors, including the Bamenda-Widikum axis in Momo division and the Bamenda-Ndop road. These restrictions significantly hindered population movements and limited the transportation of agricultural produce. The operational environment remained highly challenging and required continuous access negotiations amid a fragile, volatile, and rapidly evolving context.

items.description: Le dernier convoi de nos compatriotes contraints de quitter la Guinée-Conakry est arrivé ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026, à 18h38, au stade Général Aboubacar Sangoulé Lamizana de Bobo-Dioulasso. Cette arrivée marque l’aboutissement de la phase de rapatriement d’une vaste opération humanitaire et logistique conduite par le Gouvernement burkinabè. Parti de Bamako au Mali dans la nuit précédente, le convoi, composé d’une vingtaine d’autocars, transportait 1200 compatriotes, dont des femmes et des enfants. Plusieurs ambulances médicalisées ont également assuré le transfert de ressortissants burkinabè jusque-là hospitalisés dans des structures sanitaires de Bamako, avec un dispositif garantissant la continuité de leur prise en charge médicale. À leur arrivée, les compatriotes ont été accueillis par le Camarade Gouverneur de la région du Guiriko, en présence des autorités administratives régionales. Après plusieurs jours d’épreuve, ces compatriotes retrouvent enfin leur terre natale, entourés de la solidarité de la Nation. Avec l’arrivée de ce dernier convoi, une étape majeure vient d’être franchie. Les efforts se poursuivront désormais en faveur de l’accompagnement psychosocial, de la réunification familiale et de la réinsertion socio-économique des compatriotes de retour. L’enjeu est de faire de ce retour au pays le point de départ d’une reconstruction durable des conditions de vie de nos compatriotes. DRFS/Guiriko -DCRP/MFS L’article Retour des Burkinabè contraints de quitter la Guinée: le dernier convoi accueilli à Bobo-Dioulasso est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: World: Governments Pressed to Deliver on 250+ New Pledges at the End Violence Against Children Summit
items.description: Country: World Source: Save the Children MANILA, 18 November 2026 - Governments announced more than 250 new commitments to prevent violence against children at a key global summit on child protection in Manila, with Save the Children urging leaders to turn those promises into funded action. At the second Global Ministerial Conference to End Violence Against Children (EVAC), representatives from over 80 of the 130 countries present [1] made pledges across a range of areas, from combatting the recruitment and use of children in armed conflict and tech facilitated violence, to expanding child protection services to helping children recover from abuse. Almost 40% of the countries making pledges did so for the first time, underscoring growing global momentum to make children safer, said Save the Children. The new pledges come at a critical time for children, as conflict, climate shocks, poverty and inequality continue to expose millions of children to violence in their homes, schools, online and in their communities. Violence against children encompasses any form of physical, emotional, digital or online abuse, sexual abuse, neglect, exploitation, or harmful traditional practices directed at children. Every year, an estimated 1.6 billion children experience violence globally, including 90 million who experience sexual violence.[2], which can have lifelong consequences for children's health, learning, development, and wellbeing. While progress has been made in recent years, far too many children still face violence every day, with devastating and often lifelong consequences for their health, wellbeing and future opportunities. Save the Children urged leaders to turn promises into funded action. Rebecca Smith, Global Head of Child Protection, Save the Children, said: “We know how to prevent violence against children, now we need real commitment to make their safety a reality. These new pledges are a very welcome and important step forward, but they must now be backed by sustained investment, strong accountability and meaningful action that reaches children, wherever they live in the world, because millions of children continue to experience abuse, exploitation and harm every single day and their safety cannot be an afterthought. Children’s experiences and their voices must be at the heart of all violence prevention and survivor support initiatives.” In 2025, Save the Children’s programmes reached 5.5 million children and caregivers globally through violence prevention and response interventions. Financial stress on families can increase the risk of violence against children. Through our Money Matters Toolkit Save the Children helps caseworkers to engage families in conversations about budgeting and financial decision-making to help families make informed decisions and be more resilient. Save the Children’s Safe Families initiative works with children of all ages, caregivers and communities to support families to better communicate and solve problems together, encourage adults to better understand child development and see children as rights holders with their own views and perspectives with separate sessions just for children. ENDS Notes to editors: [1] https://www.who.int/news/item/17-11-2026-governments-make-over-230-new-pledges-to-prevent-violence-against-children [2] https://data.unicef.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/UNICEF-Data-brief-on-VAC-at-home_Nov-2025.pdf For media: Amy Sawitta Lefevre, Global Media Manager: amy.lefevre@savethechildren.org

items.title: Xi, Trump and Putin hold unprecedented trilateral summit in China
items.description: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia held their first trilateral talks on Thursday, aimed according to Beijing at “safeguarding world peace” but sparking alarm and derision elsewhere. The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, which analysts expect to be heavier in symbolism than breakthroughs, comes with Russia’s Ukraine offensive approaching the five-year mark. Trump is bogged down by his war with Iran that has choked oil supplies and pushed up consumer prices worldwide, while an ascendant China is looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. China’s President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in Shenzhen, in China’s southern Guangdong province, on November 19, 2026. — AFP The Kylin Villa summit has stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”, who responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together — for the third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting their “very special relationship”. The two men’s talks were expected to touch on trade and potentially common rules for artificial intelligence, under the cloud of the Nvidia spy scandal. “During this period, China-US relations have remained generally stable and improved, bringing tangible benefits to the people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world,” Xi said. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. Beijing, Washington and Moscow have given different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. Trump said in his meeting with Xi however that both China and the United States were “looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine.” The Kremlin has said that the agenda had not been finalised, but it would be hard to avoid discussing Ukraine at the meeting, which is set to last “no more than an hour”. Germany was also due to host Ukraine’s allies for a “Coalition of the Willing” meeting on Thursday involving envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. China has said only that the trio will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting will be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin. The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions,” said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said. Nuclear disarmament Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament , according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. “Look, we have 4,000 nuclear weapons. Russia has 3,800 nuclear weapons. China now has four or five hundred, but they’re going to catch (up),” Trump told Fox News from Shenzhen. Trump has also that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un “would like” to come to China to see him. The two met three times in Trump’s first term. Pyongyang — which has drawn closer to Russia in recent years – has not officially responded, with state media showing Kim visiting on Wednesday a naval university. Beijing on Thursday repeated that it had no information on any Kim visit. Airport welcome Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air-force flyover. This reciprocated the airport greeting Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September. “It’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship,” Trump told Fox News. Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump upon his arrival at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting on November 18, 2026 in Shenzhen, China. The airport welcome showed “great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China too,” Trump said. Other world leaders at the APEC meeting include Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, South Korea’s Lee Jae Myung, Canada’s Mark Carney and Australia’s Anthony Albanese. Takaichi, on her first visit since angering Beijing a year ago with comments about Taiwan, met Putin — relations are also tense — on Wednesday, Tokyo said. Russia’s President Vladimir Putin, China’s President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, Thailand’s Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney and Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese pose for a group photo at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, November 19, 2026. — Reuters Takaichi, who by Thursday afternoon had not held any formal meeting with Xi, said Thursday she wanted a “constructive and stable relationship” with China. Despite their differences, all the leaders — including Putin — posed for the APEC “family photo” on Thursday in special scarves. Xi opened the APEC leaders’ meeting on Thursday with a call to “reduce barriers to trade and investment”. Trump said he opposed “any form of globalist regulation or anything to control and stifle”

items.title: Côte d'Ivoire: WFP Côte d’Ivoire Women Adapt Project, November 2026 [EN/FR]
items.description: Country: Côte d'Ivoire Source: World Food Programme Please refer to the attached files. *Enhancing the climate-adaptive capacity of smallholder farming communities in the Poro Region, focusing on vulnerable women and youth* Context Climate shocks are undermining food systems in northern regions of Côte d’Ivoire, such as Poro. Since the 1980s, this region has experienced erratic rainfall patterns, resulting in repeated drought episodes and a gradual decline in average annual precipitation. These challenges are becoming more severe as temperatures continue to rise and weather patterns become less predictable. Combined with recurrent droughts and land degradation, they are significantly reducing agricultural productivity in a region where livelihoods depend heavily on rain-fed agriculture. Women farmers, who play a central role in local food systems, continue to face systemic barriers to accessing land, water, financial services, and climate information. These challenges limit their ability to adapt to climate shocks, strengthen their productivity, and build resilient livelihoods. Climate projections indicate that the share of arable land affected by drought could increase from 7% in 2000 to 23% by 2080, leading to yield declines of up to 9% for maize and 10% for millet and sorghum. This would further exacerbate food insecurity and livelihood vulnerabilities. Climate shocks are therefore not a future risk; they are a current threat to food security, livelihoods, and economic empowerment of women and youth.

items.title: I disobeyed my father’s order to delete succession video – Jimmy Odukoya
items.description: The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has admitted disobeying his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, by retaining a succession video he was instructed to delete after the founder’s successful surgery in 2021. Odukoya described his decision to keep the recording as a grave mistake while addressing about 300 church workers on Wednesday, against the backdrop of the ongoing leadership crisis at the church. He explained that his father requested the recording before travelling to the United States for surgery because he feared he might not survive the procedure. According to Church Times, which reported details of the meeting, Odukoya said he personally recorded the message in which Taiwo identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor. However, following his successful operation, the late founder reportedly asked him to erase the recording, saying the circumstances that prompted its creation no longer applied. Rather than comply, Jimmy kept the video, a decision he now acknowledges was wrong. He also claimed that only a few people, including his sisters, knew about the recording, alleging that they were responsible for making it public. The video has become central to the leadership dispute at the church, with a faction of its Board of Trustees relying on its contents to withdraw recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor. The faction announced on November 17 that it had appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, citing Taiwo’s instruction that Areogun should succeed him. In the recording, the late founder said Areogun should take over if he died or became unable to communicate, while assigning Jimmy the roles of Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the youth church. Jimmy, however, has rejected the board faction’s decision, insisting that he remains the church’s legitimate Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. He told the workers that the disagreement with the board began about a year after he assumed office, when members allegedly asked him to relinquish his position as board chairman and concentrate on pastoral responsibilities. He also alleged that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, approached him to step aside to allow her to become board chairman. The disagreement was reportedly taken to the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, after Bishop Mike Okonkwo intervened. Jimmy further denied allegations that he misappropriated N250m donated to the church for a project, maintaining that the money remained intact and that economic challenges had delayed the project. He said he had restricted access to church funds and dismissed claims of financial misconduct. Although he maintained that he remained Senior Pastor, Jimmy expressed uncertainty about the conduct of the next Sunday service and said an advertised church programme would not hold to prevent further escalation of the dispute. The post I disobeyed my father’s order to delete succession video – Jimmy Odukoya appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Les préparatifs vont bon train pour le Marathon Comar 2026
items.description: Chaque année, en cette période, les préparatifs s’accélèrent pour l’organisation du Marathon Comar Tunis-Carthage, dont la 39 e édition se tiendra le 6 décembre 2026. Alors que les coureurs d’élite fignolent leur préparation, partageant des vidéos sur les réseaux sociaux où ils donnent rendez-vous à leurs collègues bientôt à Tunis, le comité d’organisation, composé des cadres et agents des Assurances Comar et Hayett, ainsi que des représentants des institutions partenaires, met les bouchées doubles pour assurer les meilleures conditions de réussite à cette grande fête populaire, le plus important événement sportif outdoor en Tunisie et même dans la région qui attire plus de 10 000 coureurs, Tunisiens et étrangers, professionnels et amateurs, de tous âges et de toutes conditions sociales. Latif Belhedi Le comité d’organisation, présidé par Lotfi Ben Haj Kacem, également directeur des Assurances Comar, a d’ailleurs donné une conférence de presse, mercredi 18 novembre à l’hôtel Majestic, à Tunis, où il a passé en revue l’état des préparatifs, les progrès réalisés en près de quatre décennies par ce marathon emblématique inscrit sur les calendriers de l’athlétisme national et international et les nouveautés attendues pour cette édition. Jusqu’à hier matin, le nombre des inscrits dans le marathon proprement dit (42,195 Km) s’élevait 10 825, et l’on s’attend à atteindre 12 000 dans quelques jours. Le semi-marathon, antichambre de l’épreuve reine, et qui réunit les amateurs de la course à pied, connaît le même engouement avec, au jour d’hier, près de 5 300 inscrits, seuil maximal qui a obligé l’organisation à arrêter les inscriptions, sachant que le nombre total de dossards réservés à la compétition est fixé d’avance par les instances internationales, notamment l’AIMS World Running qui établit le calendrier international où le Marthon Comar est inscrit depuis sept ou huit ans. Lors de la conférence de presse, on a beaucoup appris sur les mesures prises pour assurer la réussite sur les plans sportif, organisationnel, sécuritaire, sanitaire, médiatique et même touristique et culturel, car les coureurs viennent souvent à Tunis accompagnés de leurs familles et proches. Des programmes spécifiques sont également conçus à l’intention de tous ces hôtes, sachant que les coureurs inscrits jusqu’à hier viennent de 47 pays des cinq continents. Ils sont cependant majoritairement maghrébins et européens, proximité géographique oblige. Une ambiance de fête populaire Les participants en provenance de l’Algérie voisine (près d’un millier chaque année) viennent en groupe grâce aux offres spéciales concoctées à l’occasion du Marathon Comar par les voyagistes locaux. D’où le dynamisme touristique que l’événement impulse et dont s’est félicité, lors de la conférence de presse, le représentant du ministère du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat. Les hôteliers et les restaurateurs connaissent en effet un regain d’activité les jours précédant et suivant le marathon. Les organisateurs ont beaucoup insisté sur la vocation écologique du Marathon Comar qui aime souligner sa vocation d’événement écoresponsable : nettoyage du parcours, tee-shirts officiels fabriqués à partir de matériaux recyclables, emballages respectueux de l’environnement, accessoires durables, etc., sans oublier les actions de reboisement menées par le personnel de l’entreprise dans le but de contribuer à la préservation des espaces naturels et de la biodiversité. Dans ce cadre, le Marathon Comar a aidé à planter, depuis 2021, 214 650 arbres, actions menées en partenariat avec l’association Tounes Clean Up. On apprendra aussi la constitution, grâce à la dynamique induite par le Marathon Comar, d’une association de meures d’allure, ces coureurs et coureuses expérimentés qui participent à la course, accompagnent les marathoniens, les aident à régler leur cadence de course et à utiliser intelligemment leurs ressources physiques et mentales pour atteindre la ligne d’arrivée dans les meilleures dispositions. Ayant fait leurs preuves à Tunis, ces meneurs d’allure ont été invités à participer à d’autres marathons dans la région, notamment au Maroc et au Qatar où, a expliqué la présidence de l’association lors de la conférence de presse, ils ont réussi à intéresser des coureurs et des coureuses pour venir pratiquer leur sport favori à Tunis. Toutes les conditions du succès sont réunies L’aspect sanitaire est aussi important dans un marathon que celui sportif, l’un et l’autre étant étroitement liés. Le médecin chapeautant l’équipe médicale du Marathon Comar, qui a reçu plusieurs formations internationales dans ce domaine, a expliqué que les coureurs et les coureuses, quels que soient leur sexe, leur âge ou leur condition physique, n’ont rien à craindre de prendre part à la course, car le parcours est ponctué de tentes médicales où un médecin spécialisé et des aides médicaux prennent en charge rapidement les participants ayant eu un malaise. Ils disposent d’ambulances médicalisés et de motards pour le transport et tous les équipements nécessaires à la réanimation sur place. Tout ce dispositif, ajouté aux centaines de bénévoles et d’agents de sécurité déployés sur tout le long du parcours veillent au grain pour garantir la réussite de la course sur tous les plans. L’article Les préparatifs vont bon train pour le Marathon Comar 2026 est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Nakambé : Plus de 14 radios mobilisées pour promouvoir la santé en langues nationales
items.description: La caravane de presse consacrée à la communication en santé a achevé son parcours à Tenkodogo, dans la région du Nakambé, le mercredi 18 novembre 2026. Cette dernière étape a été marquée par une émission radiophonique sur le suivi de la grossesse, une visite au centre mère-enfant. Faire de la communication un véritable outil de promotion de la santé publique. C’est l’un des objectifs poursuivis pour le mois de communication sanitaire en langue nationales. À Tenkodogo, dernière étape de cette tournée, les activités ont notamment mis l’accent sur la sensibilisation communautaire et le bilan des actions menées dans la région du Nakambé. Animation d'une émission à la radio Liberté de Parler et de Communiquer (LPC) Pour le directeur régional de la santé du Nakambé, Lendé Tougri, cette initiative constitue une innovation dans la communication sanitaire. Il s’est réjoui de la mobilisation des médias et des professionnels de santé autour des différentes thématiques abordées. « C’est une innovation en matière de communication au niveau de la santé. Avec l’accompagnement de la Direction de la communication et des relations publiques (DCRP), le mois se déroule bien. À ce jour, nous avons bénéficié de l’accompagnement de 14 radios et 14 émissions ont été réalisées sur diverses thématiques d’intérêt en santé publique », a indiqué Lendé Tougri. Ces émissions ont notamment porté sur les hépatites virales, le suivi de la grossesse, la malnutrition et la vaccination. Elles ont également été diffusées dans plusieurs langues locales, notamment le mooré, le bissa et le yana. Lendé Tougri, Directeur régional de la santé du Nakambé, explique que cette initiative constitue une innovation salutaire Au-delà de la communication, le directeur régional a également présenté les avancées enregistrées dans le secteur sanitaire au cours des quatre dernières années, selon les précisions apportées lors de son intervention. Il a fait état de 45 formations sanitaires construites, dont certaines restent à inaugurer. À ces réalisations s’ajoutent l’acquisition de 100 réfrigérateurs, de 18 ambulances, de sept groupes électrogènes, de sept véhicules de supervision ainsi que d’une radio numérique. Le renforcement des ressources humaines a également permis le recrutement de 200 nouveaux agents de santé. Il a par ailleurs souligné les efforts consentis pour renforcer la gratuité des soins, notamment en matière de dialyse. Toutefois, Lendé Tougri estime que la pérennisation de la communication demeure un défi. « On ne devrait pas attendre le mois de la communication pour communiquer. Il faut pouvoir maintenir le dialogue avec les populations et surtout avec les hommes des médias », a-t-il souligné. Photo de famille après l’émission à la radio Liberté de Parler et de Communiquer (LPC) La sensibilisation s’est également poursuivie sur les ondes de la radio Liberté de Parler et de Communiquer (LPC), à travers une émission consacrée au suivi de la grossesse, de 10h à 11h. À cette occasion, Sabine T. Zemba/Sawadogo, attachée de soins en gynécologie, a entretenu les auditeurs sur l’importance des consultations prénatales dès le début de la grossesse. « Dès que la femme se rend compte qu’elle est enceinte, elle doit se rendre dans le centre de santé le plus proche pour qu’on puisse confirmer la grossesse. Dès lors qu’elle est confirmée, les consultations prénatales doivent commencer, ainsi que les vaccinations et la prise des médicaments nécessaires », a-t-elle expliqué. La caravane s’est également poursuivie par une visite au centre mère-enfant de Tenkodogo. À cette occasion, l’infirmier chef de poste, Adama Kobiane, a expliqué que la sensibilisation en langues locales constitue déjà une pratique au sein de sa structure. « Nous sommes une structure tellement proche de la population que nous sommes obligés de nous adapter à ses besoins. Nous travaillons depuis longtemps sur différentes thématiques dans les langues locales. Ce mois formalisé vient donc en appui à ce que nous faisons déjà », a-t-il souligné. Justine Sandwidi, l’une des personnes sensibilisées par le centre mère-enfant, témoigne des changements observés dans les habitudes d’hygiène au sein de sa communauté. Justine Sandwidi, l’une des personnes sensibilisées par le centre mère-enfant témoigne des avantages de la sensibilisation « On nous a recommandé de garder nos maisons propres et de ne pas laisser les eaux usées stagner dans les cours. Nous avons appliqué ces conseils et nous constatons aujourd’hui leurs avantages, notamment dans la prévention de certaines maladies comme le paludisme et la dengue. Nous remercions le gouvernement pour cette initiative et demandons que les sensibilisations se poursuivent », a-t-elle confié. Cette étape à Tenkodogo a ainsi marqué la fin de l’immersion de la caravane de presse dans les différentes localités visitées. De Ziniaré à Fada N’Gourma, en passant par Tenkodogo, cette immersion a mis en évidence la place des langues nationales dans la sensibilisation et la nécessité de maintenir le dialogue entre les services de santé et les populations au-delà du mois de la communication sanitaire en langues nationales. Sakinatou ZOUNDI Minute.bf

items.title: Lombrices, hongos y orina para cultivar patatas en la mala tierra de la Luna
items.description: En 2032 ya habrá agricultores en la Luna. Ese es, al menos, el objetivo de la NASA. Para entonces, el Programa Artemis prevé que, entre las tres primeras misiones de la base que planean instalar en el polo sur del satélite, esté el proyecto LEAF (hoja en inglés, pero también acrónimo de Efectos Lunares en la Flora Agrícola). La prioridad que dan al cultivo tiene todo el sentido: sin producción local, ni la colonización de la Luna, ni el viaje posterior a Marte parecen posibles. Por eso, las distintas agencias espaciales están impulsando proyectos de agricultura extraterrestre. Uno de ellos acaba de publicar sus primeros resultados: han logrado una buena cosecha de patatas, pero solo tras dopar la mala tierra lunar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: India: LOCAL Alert 001: Cyclone Akva​n - Third Cyclone in 24 Days - Pre-landfall update as of 18 November 2026, 1:30 pm IST · Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha
items.description: Country: India Source: Humanitarian Aid International Please refer to the attached file. OVERVIEW Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan lay about 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam at 5:30 am on 18 November, moving north-northwest at only about 3 km/h. It is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on 20 November, with winds of 100-110 km/h gusting to 120 km/h; earlier bulletins had expected a very severe cyclonic storm with winds of 145 km/h. Akvan is the third cyclone to strike this coast in 24 days, after Arnab (28 October) and Murasu (3 November). All 10 districts on red or orange alert were hit by those storms, seven of them by both.

items.title: Statement: USCRI Urges European Countries to Stop Plans to Send People Who Sought Asylum to Rwanda
items.description: Countries: Rwanda, Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Netherlands, World Source: US Committee for Refugees and Immigrants On November 16, 2026, five European countries announced plans to send people who sought asylum in Europe and cannot be returned to their home country to Rwanda. The “Group of Five”—which includes Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Greece, and Denmark—states that it will send people whose asylum claims have been adjudicated and denied to a return hub overseas because they have no right to stay in Europe. The enforcement of returns should not come at the cost of eroding human rights for migrants, refugees, and asylum seekers. USCRI strongly urges the “Group of Five” to retract their deal with Rwanda and stop pursuing return hubs. Return hubs expose vulnerable groups to the danger of refoulement, or the forcible return of a person to a country where they face a risk of persecution, torture, or serious harm. The principle of non-refoulement is a core human rights guarantee that is enshrined in several key international treaties, including the 1951 Refugee Convention. “The Group of Five is attempting to skirt this international legal and moral obligation by sending people to a country where they have no ties and will feel pressured to either face the danger of an unfamiliar legal process in Rwanda or face the danger of returning to the place where they fled,” said Eskinder Negash, President and CEO of the U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI). This announcement follows a meeting in September between the Group of Five, where they announced intentions to pursue a deal with a non-European country to host migrant return hubs. Despite legal controversy surrounding return hubs, the European Parliament adopted regulation in June 2026 allowing countries to pursue deals to establish them. “The idea of sending anyone who fled their country to seek safety to an offshore site should be against our moral principles as an international community,” Negash continued. “Global coordination should be in pursuit of protecting people who face danger, rather than exposing them to more risks.” Deals with Rwanda on migration have been widely criticized. In July 2024, a deal between the United Kingdom and Rwanda to send asylum seekers for processing was scrapped after heavy scrutiny from human rights advocates and international human rights organizations . Rwanda has reportedly received $7.5 million from the United States to accept third country removals, a practice that is currently subject to legal challenge. The Group of Five stated that it is working with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and the International Organization for Migration . Both organizations have stated that human rights must be guaranteed and that they will engage with the countries as they move forward. USCRI is closely tracking these developments. The danger of globally institutionalizing third country returns is at risk. Follow these developments through The Legal Landscape or USCRI’s Third Country Deportations Tracker .

items.title: Bourse de Casablanca : ouverture en grise mine
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca, fermée mercredi à l'occasion de la Fête de l'Indépendance, a démarré en grise mine jeudi, son indice phare, le MASI, reculant de 0,29% à 17.184,77 points (pts). Le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, cédait 0,65% à 1.293,92 pts, alors que le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, prenait 0,17% à 1.274,91 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, progressait de 0,02% à 1.632,94 pts. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes baisses étaient accusées par Managem (-4,61% à 1.303 DH), SMI (-3,52% à 4.600 DH), Minière Touissit (-1,82% à 3.448 DH), Résidences Dar Saada (-1,55% à 171,2 DH) et Addoha (-1,28% à 38,5 DH). À l'opposé, Stroc Industrie (+5,88% à 162 DH), IB Maroc.com (+5,16% à 55 DH), Jet Energy (+4,21% à 198 DH), SNEP (+2,44% à 252 DH) et Jet Contractors (+2,08% à 1.620 DH) réalisaient les meilleures performances. Mardi, le MASI avait clôturé sur une perte de 0,03%. The post Bourse de Casablanca : ouverture en grise mine appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Navy’s combat capabilities significantly enhanced across all operational domains: Admiral Ashraf
items.description: Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Naveed Ashraf on Thursday said the Pakistan Navy has significantly enhanced its combat capabilities across all operational domains. He made the remarks while addressing the graduation parade of the Pakistan Air Force Academy Asghar Khan in Risalpur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Nowshera district. CNS Admiral Ashraf stated that the Pakistan Navy was making significant headway towards modernising its fleet. “The induction of state-of-the-art warships, Hangor-class submarines , indigenously developed long-range weapons, unmanned systems, and the establishment of Pakistan Maritime Science & Technology Park are some of the important developments taking place,” he highlighted. The naval chief further said that the navy’s combat capabilities “have recently undergone significant enhancement and transformation across all operational domains aligned with contemporary and future warfare demands”. The navy is set to induct a total of eight Hangor-class submarines. The first one arrived at Karachi Port in June and conducted its maiden live weapon firing in the Arabian Sea in September. In mid-April, the Pakistan Navy fired a locally developed anti-ship ballistic missile to engage targets at an extended range. Days later, it conducted a successful test of an indigenously developed anti-ship weapon system, Taimoor. In November last year, the navy conducted a successful test of an indigenously developed ship-launched anti-ship ballistic missile. Speaking at the parade, CNS Ashraf noted that the character of modern warfare has altered dramatically and is “evolving at an unprecedented pace”. “One of the key factors behind this transformation is the emergence of new technologies. As such, warfare today is closely linked with technology, leading to revolutionary changes in concepts, doctrines and organisational restructuring,” he explained. Admiral Ashraf pointed out that conflicts were no longer restricted to traditional battlefields, and spanned the electronic warfare, cyber, space and cognitive domains. “More so, autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, and information warfare have reshaped the very texture of how battles are fought and won,” he added. ‘Multifaceted security challenges’ Admiral Ashraf noted that the global and regional strategic environment has become more complex, particularly in the backdrop of heightened tensions in the Middle East. “Geopolitical dynamics are shifting rapidly, presenting multifaceted security challenges that demand constant vigilance, strategic foresight, and remarkable operational readiness to deter conventional, as well as hybrid and asymmetric threats,” the naval chief noted. He affirmed that the armed forces “are fully cognisant of such developments and have prepared accordingly”. He further stated that Operation Muhafizul Bahr , initiated in March this year when the Middle East conflict sparked, was still “continuing successfully”. CNS Ashraf highlighted that the armed forces were “invincible and capable to deter any aggression”, recalling the May 2025 Pakistan-India conflict . The Pakistan Army had named the period of conflict with India, from the April 22 Pahalgam attack to the May 10 conclusion of Operation Bunyanum Marsoos, as Marka-i-Haq in May. “I am sure our adversary has learned the lesson, and it would be unwise to need a second,” he remarked, lauding the air force’s “extraordinary performance”. He added: “For the first time in the history of warfare, the Pakistan Air Force conducted multi-domain operations chiefly comprising indigenous capabilities, especially the homegrown kill chain that was the highlight of the whole conflict and the outcome of a very aggressive, innovative, and prudent strategy of modernisation and indigenisation in the past few years.” Narrating the navy’s performance, Admiral Ashraf said the Pakistan Navy “successfully deterred the Indian Navy from any hostilities at sea and it remained at bay throughout the conflict”. The naval chief described the air force and navy as “brothers in arms”, with the “maritime domain as our shared operational space”. “It is here we exercise together and shall fight alongside each other to defend our motherland. God willing, together we shall prove equal to the task,” he affirmed. CNS Ashraf maintained that Pakistan is a “peace-loving nation and always stands resolute to prioritise restraint, dialogue, diplomacy, regional stability and world peace”. However, he added, “But we know how to defend our motherland. In consistent pursuit of peace, our country and armed forces have rendered matchless sacrifices. We, as a nation, stand fully determined to continue our efforts until peace and stability are established in the region.” The naval chief appreciated the presence of Turkiye’s air force chief, General Rafet Dalkiran, at the parade. “We are proud of our time-tested friendship with Türkiye, as the two nations have always stood shoulder to shoulder in every thick and thin,” he added. Concluding his address, the naval chief congratulated the graduating cadets.

items.title: Kusal Mendis departs after fifty as Sri Lanka take 14-run lead against Pakistan in second Test
items.description: Sri Lanka fought back from a difficult position to take a 14-run overall lead against Pakistan, reaching 241-6 at tea on the third day of the second Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday. The visitors added 167 runs during the day for the loss of three wickets, recovering from 74-3 at the start of play. Captain Kusal Mendis led the resistance with a half-century before falling to Salman Ali Agha, while Sonal Dinusha and Milan Rathnayake remained unbeaten at the interval. Pakistan had secured a commanding 227-run first-innings lead after bowling Sri Lanka out for 98 and then making 325 in reply. The hosts had strengthened their position further by reducing the visitors to 74-3 at stumps on the second day. Resuming on Thursday, Sri Lanka lost both overnight batters as Pakistan’s fast bowlers struck in the morning session. Aamer Jamal dismissed Dhananjaya de Silva for 37, trapping him lbw with a sharp incoming delivery. The batter reviewed the decision but the original call was upheld. De Silva had struck six fours in his 47-ball innings and his departure left Sri Lanka at 99-4. Razaullah then ended Pasindu Sooriyabandara’s resistance, having the batter caught behind by wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori for 38 off 116 deliveries. Sooriyabandara, who struck three fours, had battled for nearly two hours before edging a delivery down the leg side. Sri Lanka reached lunch at 166-5, having added 92 runs in the morning session. Kusal was unbeaten on 32, with Dinusha on 19, and the pair continued their recovery after the break. Kusal completed his 24th Test half-century, scoring 53 from 126 balls with eight fours. He and Dinusha put together an 81-run partnership before Salman provided Pakistan with their only breakthrough of the afternoon. In the 70th over, Kusal attempted a sweep against the off-spinner but played the ball onto his leg stump, departing at 215-6. His dismissal gave Pakistan a much-needed wicket after a prolonged period of resistance. Dinusha, however, continued to frustrate the hosts, reaching 46 not out from 101 deliveries, with six boundaries. He was struck on the hand by a rising delivery from Jamal during the afternoon but continued after receiving treatment. Rathnayake joined him following Kusal’s dismissal and scored an unbeaten 17 off 16 balls, including three fours. The pair added 26 runs for the seventh wicket to take Sri Lanka to 241-6 at tea. Pakistan continued to miss the services of Saqib Khan, who has been ruled out of further bowling after sustaining a left hamstring strain on Wednesday. With the new ball due after 80 overs, Pakistan will seek quick wickets in the final session, while Sri Lanka will aim to extend their lead through Dinusha and Rathnayake.

items.title: Défaite de l’équipe d’Algérie face au Togo : Maamar Djebbour charge la FAF
items.description: Sortie au vitriol de Maamar Djebbour. Le journaliste vétéran de la chaîne III de la radio algérienne n’a pas mâché ses mots au lendemain de la lourde défaite de l’équipe d’Algérie de football, mardi 17 novembre, face au Togo en éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 (3-0). Djebbour reproche notamment à la Fédération algérienne de football (FAF) de s'être précipitée dans le choix du staff technique après la coupe du monde 2026. Mais avant cela, la FAF avait commis, selon le journaliste sportif, une autre erreur en prolongeant juste avant le mondial le contrat de l'ancien sélectionneur Vladimir Petkovic, pour le limoger après la compétition en lui payant de fortes indemnités. Choix du staff technique : “ Le président de la FAF a agi seul ” La “ deuxième erreur ” était de “ sortir du chapeau, comme un magicien ”, l'entraîneur Brahim Hemdani , parce qu'il avait “ gagné la médaille d’or aux Jeux méditerranéens ” 2026. “ Mais soyons sérieux, c'est un niveau différent, c'est une équipe nationale ”, dit Maamar Djebbour, qui reproche au président de la Fédération, Walid Sadi, qui est par ailleurs ministre des Sports, d’avoir agi seul, “ sans consulter personne ”. “ Nul n’a été consulté, c'est le seul choix du président de la FAF. Peut-être qu'on lui a susurré à l’oreille au niveau de la DTN, et j’en doute, un choix qui nous a menés à taper le mur ”, a-t-il dénoncé. Selon Maamar Djebbour, une réunion est prévue au niveau de la FAF et “ Hemdani sera sacrifié ”. Mais, s’est-il demandé, “ qui doit rendre des comptes après cette débâcle, après cette triste mascarade ? ” La réponse est, pour lui, évidente : “C'est le président de la Fédération algérienne de football ” qui doit “ assumer seul ” parce qu'il est “ le seul responsable de ce choix ”. Hafid Derradji impute lui aussi une part de responsabilité à la Fédération “ On ne joue pas avec une nation, on ne joue pas avec son équipe nationale, on doit la protéger ”, s’est écrié Maamar Djebbour, d'autant plus que, a-t-il rappelé, le président de la République a demandé à “mettre l'équipe nationale dans de meilleures conditions ”. “ Malheureusement, ceux qui sont censés traduire la volonté politique du chef de l'État ne l’ont pas fait ”, a-t-il regretté. Moins virulent, le journaliste algérien de beINSPORTS, Hafid Derradji, a lui aussi imputé à la Fédération une part de la responsabilité des résultats de l’équipe nationale. “ Le maintien ou le départ du staff technique actuel ne résoudra pas définitivement le problème (…) car les joueurs aussi ont leur part de responsabilité au même titre que la Fédération ”, a écrit Derradji dans un article publié dans le journal londonien El Quds Al Arabi. L’article Défaite de l’équipe d'Algérie face au Togo : Maamar Djebbour charge la FAF est apparu en premier sur TSA .

10 killed as Karachi-bound passenger coach, LPG bowser collide on Makran coastal highway near Ormara
items.description: GWADAR: At least 10 people, including a woman and a child, were killed and several others sustained burn injuries when a Karachi-bound passenger coach collided with a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) bowser and caught fire near Basol in Ormara on Thursday, police said. Superintendent of Police (SP) Makran Coastal Highway Police Muhammad Aslam Bangulzai confirmed the death toll, saying the coach was travelling from Turbat to Karachi when the collision occurred. “The impact triggered a fire that quickly engulfed both vehicles, trapping passengers inside,” he added. Rescue teams, coastal highway police personnel and local administration officials rushed to the scene, while the injured were taken to the Ormara Health Centre for treatment, Bangulzai said. He added that traffic on the Makran Coastal Highway remained suspended for several hours following the accident, leaving long queues of vehicles stranded near Basol and Ormara. In a similar incident in August, six members of a family were burnt to death after a speeding gas bowser hit their car head-on and overturned on the coastal highway in the Ormara area of Gwadar district. In March, seven people, including a child, were killed and eight others injured in a head-on collision between two vehicles on the coastal highway. In January, a passenger vehicle overturned on the coastal highway in Ormara, killing 10 people and leaving more than 30 others injured.
